subject: Architecture
title: The Charles Bridge: Prague's Medieval Marvel
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Charles Bridge: Prague's Medieval Marvel.

hook.text: Legend says eggs were mixed into the mortar of Prague's Charles Bridge. Scientists found it's actually true.

buildup.text: Construction began in 1357 under Charles IV. Sixteen stone arches span 1,693 feet across the Vltava River.

discovery.text: Thirty Baroque statues line the bridge — saints, angels, and a golden cross mark this open-air gallery.

twist.text: Protein from eggs in the mortar actually improves durability — the bridge has survived 660 years of floods.

climax.text: Today 30,000 tourists cross it daily. Charles IV laid the first stone at 5:31 AM — an astrologically chosen time.

punchline.text: Eggs, astrology, and Gothic stonework. Prague's oldest bridge still stands.

quiz.question: What unusual ingredient was mixed into the Charles Bridge's mortar?
options: Eggs, which improved the mortar's durability

details.summary: The Charles Bridge in Prague, completed around 1402, has survived floods, wars, and six centuries of continuous use. Its 16 arches span the Vltava River using a sandstone structure so robust that it supported motor vehicles until 1965 — a load its medieval builders never imagined.
details.whyItMatters: The Charles Bridge demonstrates medieval engineering's remarkable durability. Designed with empirical knowledge rather than modern calculations, it has outlasted countless modern structures.
takeaways: It supported motor vehicles until 1965 despite medieval origins
Six centuries of continuous use prove exceptional durability

faq.question: Is it true that eggs were used in the mortar?
faq.answer: Legend claims egg yolks were added to strengthen the mortar. Scientific analysis of the mortar has found organic compounds that could be egg protein, though the evidence is inconclusive. Medieval builders did sometimes add organic materials to improve mortar workability.

faq.question: How has the Charles Bridge survived so many floods?
faq.answer: Its massive piers with ice-breaking cutwater profiles deflect water and debris. The arches are semi-circular, providing generous clearance for floodwater. Several arches have been rebuilt after major floods, but the overall structure has proven remarkably resilient across centuries.
